problem.name: Basis representation of a finite black-box ring
problem.name_latex: Basis representation of a finite black-box ring
problem.statement_latex: Given generators of a finite ring $R$ and uniquely encoded addition and multiplication oracles, compute an additive invariant-factor basis and the multiplication structure constants in that basis. Complexity is in $\log|R|$ and the generator-description length.
problem.statement_text: Given generators of a finite ring $R$ and uniquely encoded addition and multiplication oracles, compute an additive invariant-factor basis and the multiplication structure constants in that basis. Complexity is in $\log|R|$ and the generator-description length.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.
evidence.description_text: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.
hardware.description_text: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|R|)$ quantum time by Arvind--Das--Mukhopadhyay, using abelian-group decomposition and quantum discrete logarithms.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|R|)$ quantum time by Arvind–Das–Mukhopadhyay, using abelian-group decomposition and quantum discrete logarithms.

classical.headline_latex: Generic additive-group structure and discrete-logarithm algorithms give $\widetilde O(|R|^{1/2})$ ring operations, with polynomially many basis products. If structure constants are supplied initially, the basis-conversion work is already present in the input.
classical.headline_text: Generic additive-group structure and discrete-logarithm algorithms give $\widetilde O(|R|^{1/2})$ ring operations, with polynomially many basis products. If structure constants are supplied initially, the basis-conversion work is already present in the input.
